parsed.explanation: The quoted König's-lemma paragraph does not deliver a valid contradiction. The pruning/contraction rules govern nodes of the actual tree, whose labels are the branch elements x_1, x_2, ...; the argument 'inserts c' into an object the tree never built. The needed contradiction would require that some minimal transversal extending a prefix {x_1,...,x_k} must contain c, but nothing shown forces this: such a minimal transversal can meet F_{k_1} (which is disjoint only from the prefix up to k_1) at any element beyond that prefix, not specifically at c. Hence 'the element selected there is dispensable' holds only for the artificially modified branch-plus-c, not for any node of the pruned tree, and no conflict with the pruning rule follows. Moreover 'dispensable' and 'contract' are never defined precisely enough to check the argument. Since the finiteness of the minimal transversals B_1,...,B_s — the sole source of the finite modulus L — rests entirely on this paragraph, the finiteness obligation is unproven as written.
